title: It’s a Thin Line Between Love and Hate: Using the Echo in Modeling Dynamics of Racist Online Communities
findings: The paper found that a multi-modal neural architecture, combining textual analysis (BERT, BiLSTM) with social network structure, can effectively detect and classify users promoting antisemitic hate speech via the ambiguous '(((echo)))' meme. The study revealed a strong 'intersectionality of hate,' where users promoting antisemitism also frequently target other groups, such as Muslims and Arabs. The research also traced the semantic drift of the antisemitic symbol from marking specific Jewish individuals to more abstract concepts central to antisemitic conspiracy theories (e.g., 'globalists'). Furthermore, hate-mongering communities were found to be tightly-knit and organized within their own networks, despite having fewer overall social connections than mainstream users.
